claim: The League of Nations, which could not keep great powers inside, had none of the major powers as members by the start of WWII; the veto was designed to avoid that fate
author: Sara Davies and Alex Bellamy
credentials: Davies: ARC Future Fellow, Griffith University; Bellamy: Professor of International Security, Griffith University
title: Don’t be too quick to condemn the UN Security Council power of veto
quote: Washington argued that a world organisation that hinged on ongoing participation of the great powers must allow them to protect their “vital interests” or fall into irrelevance. This proved to the case for the UN’s predecessor, the League of Nations ... By the time it was most needed, at the onset of the Second World War, none of the most significant world powers (US, USSR, Germany, Japan) were members.

claim: The US itself said in 1944 it would not stay in the UN for a day without the veto
author: Stewart M. Patrick
credentials: Senior fellow, Council on Foreign Relations (international institutions and global governance)
title: Here's Why the UN Sat on Its Hands During 5 Years of War in Syria - Defense One
quote: During the Dumbarton Oaks conference of 1944, a U.S. senator complained to Secretary of State Cordell Hull that the emerging blueprint for the UN Security Council constituted “a discrimination against small nations.” Hull replied bluntly that the United States “would not remain there for a day without retaining its veto power.”

claim: The veto exists so the UN cannot authorize war against a great power's wishes, reducing the likelihood of major war among great powers
author: Stewart M. Patrick
credentials: Senior fellow, Council on Foreign Relations (international institutions and global governance)
title: Here's Why the UN Sat on Its Hands During 5 Years of War in Syria - Defense One
quote: The rationale for the veto was plain: no structure of peace could be viable if war could be authorized contrary to the expressed wishes of one of the world’s policemen. ... It is rigged to advance the interests of the great powers—and to reduce the likelihood that major war will break out among them. The system provides a baseline order. That is nothing to sneeze at, given the horrors of the First and Second World Wars.

claim: Great powers will not accept binding authority without the veto, so the alternative to the veto is no Security Council
author: David Bosco
credentials: Professor, Indiana University Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies; author on the history of the Security Council
title: In defense of the veto power – Foreign PolicySearch IconShare iconCopy Link iconEmail iconFacebook iconBluesky iconX iconLinkedIn iconWhatsApp iconReddit iconSave iconDownload iconCopy Link iconEmail
quote: Perhaps the most fundamental point about the veto is that you could not have a Security Council without it. Major powers will simply not grant an international body binding legal authority on matters of peace and security unless they are certain that it will not prejudice their interests. So the alternative to the Security Council veto is really no Security Council, or at least not in a recognizable form.

claim: In January 2026 the US withdrew from 31 UN-linked entities it said no longer serve American interests - great powers exit UN bodies today, even with the veto intact
author: Anadolu Agency
credentials: Turkish state news agency; original reporting of the UN spokesperson's statement
title: UN chief 'regrets' US decision to withdraw from international organizations
quote: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Thursday lamented the latest decision by the Trump administration to withdraw from 31 entities linked to the organization. ... The UN reaction came after the White House late Wednesday announced US President Donald Trump's signing of a "Presidential Memorandum" directing government agencies to withdraw from 66 international organizations that the administration argued are no longer serving American interests.

claim: Empirical research finds peacekeeping is strongly associated with peace (reduced violence), despite known problems
author: Barbara F. Walter, Lise Morje Howard and V. Page Fortna
credentials: Political scientists at UC San Diego, Georgetown and Columbia; peer-reviewed review of the peacekeeping literature
title: The Extraordinary Relationship between Peacekeeping and Peace
quote: Numerous empirical studies have examined the role of third-party peacekeeping in reducing violence around the world. Their results reveal an extraordinary relationship between peacekeepers and peace, notwithstanding a number of well-known problems.

claim: Security Council decisions bind every UN member (Article 25)
author: United Nations
publication: Charter of the United Nations, Article 25
title: Chapter V: The Security Council (Articles 23-32) | United Nations
quote: The Members of the United Nations agree to accept and carry out the decisions of the Security Council in accordance with the present Charter.
